insights.concise_text: QRNNs address standard RNNs' inability to parallelize very long sequences by allowing parallel computation across timestep and minibatch dimensions while preserving sequence order.

triple.subject: QRNNs
triple.object: standard RNNs, including LSTMs, on very long sequences

insights.concise_text: QRNNs combine CNNs' increased parallelism and better scaling to long sequences with RNN-like dependence on overall sequence order.

triple.subject: QRNNs
triple.object: CNNs' parallelism and RNN-like sequence order dependence

insights.concise_text: The QRNN's convolutional and pooling subcomponents jointly explain its parallel computation across timestep and minibatch dimensions.

triple.subject: QRNN convolutional and pooling subcomponents
triple.object: parallel computation across timestep and minibatch dimensions

insights.concise_text: Because QRNNs lack recurrent weights, variational inference–based dropout does not apply, so zoneout was extended to the QRNN architecture.

triple.subject: QRNNs lacking recurrent weights
triple.object: extended zoneout instead of variational inference–based dropout

insights.concise_text: The zoneout extension described for QRNNs was applied on the Penn Treebank as dropout with ratio 0.1 on the forget gates of the QRNN.

triple.subject: zoneout extension to QRNNs
triple.object: Penn Treebank (PTB)

insights.concise_text: On the Penn Treebank, applying a small amount of zoneout removed the need for early stopping and achieved competitive perplexity to the variational LSTM of BIBREF13.

triple.subject: zoneout on the QRNN
triple.object: no early stopping and competitive levels of perplexity to the variational LSTM of BIBREF13

insights.concise_text: The QRNN's negligible recurrent pooling computation on long sequences is reflected on Penn Treebank by the “RNN” layers no longer being the bottleneck.

triple.subject: negligible recurrent pooling computation
triple.object: the “RNN” layers to no longer be the bottleneck on Penn Treebank

insights.concise_text: The sequence-to-sequence QRNN architecture evaluated on IWSLT German–English spoken-domain translation uses a QRNN encoder and a modified QRNN, enhanced with attention, as decoder.

triple.subject: sequence-to-sequence QRNN architecture
triple.object: IWSLT German–English spoken-domain translation

insights.concise_text: The modified decoder that supplements convolution outputs with the final encoder hidden state avoids the representational-power limitation of feeding only the last encoder hidden state into recurrent pooling.

triple.subject: modified QRNN decoder
triple.object: limited representational power from feeding only the last encoder hidden state into recurrent pooling

insights.concise_text: On IWSLT German–English spoken-domain translation, the QRNN outperformed the character-level LSTM and almost matched a word-level attentional baseline.

triple.subject: QRNN
triple.object: character-level LSTM on IWSLT German–English spoken-domain translation
